content.user_title: Integrate Better Auth with Next.js App Router
content.value_statement: Next.js teams need reliable authentication patterns that work with the App Router. This skill guides Better Auth setup, sessions, protected routes, hooks, and testing checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when Better Auth fits a Next.js App Router project.
Outlines Better Auth initialization, providers, callbacks, and database adapter planning.
Guides JWT token settings, expiration, refresh behavior, and secure transmission.
Explains session access across server components, client components, hooks, and layouts.
Describes protected route behavior through middleware, redirects, and unauthorized states.
Lists security, performance, error handling, and testing considerations for authentication flows.
limitations: The skill is conceptual and does not include executable implementation files.
It targets the Next.js App Router and does not cover Pages Router projects.
It assumes Better Auth is installed and compatible with the project database strategy.
Project-specific provider settings, schemas, and deployment policies still require validation.

use_cases.title: Plan App Router Authentication
use_cases.description: Define the Better Auth components, session access points, middleware behavior, and protected pages for a new Next.js product.

use_cases.title: Review Session Architecture
use_cases.description: Check whether server components, client hooks, JWT settings, cookies, and redirects follow a consistent authentication design.

use_cases.title: Prepare Auth Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Create test scenarios for sign in, session persistence, protected route access, token handling, and authentication error states.

prompt_templates.title: Map My Auth Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new application
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a Better Auth setup for my Next.js App Router project. Include required files, providers, session flow, and protected route decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Protected Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design protected routes for my App Router application. Explain middleware checks, redirects, server component access, and client loading states.

prompt_templates.title: Review Session Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Better Auth session design. Check JWT lifetime, refresh behavior, secure cookie use, server access, hook usage, and logout cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Auth Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to prepare a release checklist for Better Auth in Next.js. Cover CSRF protection, rate limiting, secret storage, error handling, performance, and tests.

output_examples.input: I need authentication for a new App Router dashboard.
output: A recommended Better Auth setup path with provider, database, session, and middleware decisions.
A list of protected routes and expected redirect behavior for unauthenticated users.
Security checks for cookies, secrets, CSRF protection, and rate limiting.

output_examples.input: My app has session bugs between server and client views.
output: A review plan for server component session access and client hook synchronization.
Likely failure points for loading states, expired sessions, refresh behavior, and logout cleanup.
Testing steps for session persistence across requests and route changes.

output_examples.input: We are preparing Better Auth for production.
output: A production readiness checklist for secrets, secure cookies, callbacks, token settings, and auth endpoints.
Performance considerations for middleware session lookup and token validation.
Error handling requirements for failed sign in, expired sessions, and provider outages.

best_practices: Store authentication secrets in a secure environment manager and rotate them through a documented process.
Use server components for trusted session checks and client components for interactive authentication UI.
Test sign in, sign out, session expiration, route protection, and social provider failure paths.
anti_patterns: Do not place sensitive session tokens in client-readable storage when secure HTTP-only cookies are available.
Do not protect routes only with client-side checks because users can bypass rendered UI state.
Do not launch authentication without validating redirects, callback URLs, CSRF handling, and rate limits.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete Better Auth implementation?
faq.answer: No. It provides conceptual guidance and checklists for implementation in a Next.js App Router project.

faq.question: Can I use this with the Next.js Pages Router?
faq.answer: No. The skill is written for App Router patterns and server components.

faq.question: Does it cover social login?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes social provider planning, callback settings, and related authentication flow considerations.

faq.question: Does it handle JWT configuration?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers token generation, validation, expiration, refresh behavior, claims, signing, and secure transmission.

faq.question: What security topics are included?
faq.answer: It covers secure cookies, CSRF protection, input validation, rate limiting, secret management, and session invalidation.
